#DantePH Update (as of 5 p.m., 22 July 2025)
The low pressure area east of Aurora developed into tropical depression Dante.
Dante is not seen to make landfall but will enhance the southwest monsoon or habagat through Friday, July 25.
No wind signals are expected to be hoisted.
The enhanced habagat will bring significant rainfall over Luzon and some parts of Visayas.
Up to torrential rains may be expected over Pangasinan, Zambales, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Metro Manila.
Serious threats of flooding and landslides remain.
Dante was spotted 1,130 km east of Northern Luzon at 4 p.m. Tuesday, with winds of 45 kph and gusts up to 55 kph. It is moving north northwestward at 20 kph.
The disturbance will intensify up to tropical storm strength while moving northwestward over the Philippine Sea.
It may exit the Philippine area of responsibility late Thursday or early Friday.
Meanwhile, the low pressure area near Batanes may either merge with the broader circulation of Dante or cross Extreme Northern Luzon towards the northern West Philippine Sea. #WeatherPatrol | via Ariel Rojas, ABS-CBN News

While rainwater is naturally pure, the first rain can be particularly problematic due to contaminants it may carry. Here are some reasons why bathing in the rain might not be ideal ¹ ²: - *Pollutants and toxins*: The first rain can wash away dirt, pollutants, and residues from the atmosphere and surface runoffs, making it potentially acidic and harmful to the skin. These pollutants can cause skin irritation, allergic reactions, and other health issues. - *Microorganisms*: Rainwater can contain bacteria, viruses, and parasites that can cause waterborne diseases like cholera, typhoid, and diarrhea. These microorganisms can also lead to skin infections and other health problems. - *Skin issues*: Prolonged exposure to rainwater can strip the skin of its natural oils, leading to dryness and irritation. Some people might experience skin rashes, fungal infections, or other skin conditions due to the pollutants and bacteria in rainwater. - *Respiratory problems*: Breathing in polluted air during the first rain can trigger respiratory issues, especially for people with asthma or other pre-existing conditions. - *Hypothermia*: Taking a cold shower or bath, especially during rainy weather, can lower body temperature significantly and increase the risk of hypothermia.

Heavy rain and floods have not stopped a Filipina entrepreneur in the northern Philippines from continuing with her online live-streaming sales while standing submerged in waist-high waters.
Maica Mendoza took advantage of the floods on Friday, July 25, by showcasing her waders live through an online shopping platform, believing that seeing how her items work in the real-life scenario would boost her sales.
Mendoza’s unique live-selling strategy, which she said started back in 2020, has garnered a steady following of over 32,000 followers on TikTok. She lives in Calumpit, Bulacan, which is prone to floods during typhoon or monsoon seasons.
Typhoon #EmongPH made landfall in the province of Pangasinan early morning Friday and has since weakened to a tropical storm after crossing the mountainous region and exiting the landmass of Luzon.

The Duterte brand of leadership ay isang makapangyarihan at mapagpalayang pamumuno na tunay na nagbago sa takbo ng kasaysayan ng Pilipinas. Mula sa pagiging Mayor ng Davao na kilala sa disiplina at tapang, dinala ni Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte ang kanyang malasakit at political will sa buong bansa. Hindi siya natakot harapin ang mga oligarko, sindikato, at mga abusadong opisyal. Tinulungan niya maging ang mga politiko na kalauna’y tumalikod sa kanya, kabilang na ang pamilya Marcos, at sa kanyang panahon, ibinalik sa Libingan ng mga Bayani ang labi ni Marcos Sr., isang makasaysayang hakbang na tinanggihan ng mga naunang administrasyon. Sa ilalim ng kanyang liderato, umusbong ang Build Build Build program na nagpatayo ng libo-libong imprastruktura gaya ng expressways, airports tulad ng Bicol International Airport, daan-daang tulay, bypass roads, flood control projects, at maging ang kauna-unahang subway ng Pilipinas. Tumaas ang suweldo ng mga sundalo, pulis, at guro. Sa gitna ng pandemya, matagumpay na nailunsad ang vaccination rollout, naipanalo ang laban sa kaguluhan, at naipamahagi ang ayuda sa milyon-milyong Pilipino. Nilansag niya ang mga teroristang Maute at Abu Sayyaf sa Marawi, pinamunuan ang rehabilitasyon ng lungsod, at isinulong ang localized peace talks sa mga rebeldeng komunista. Sa pamamagitan ng NTF-ELCAC, libo-libong dating NPA fighters ang sumuko at binigyan ng kabuhayan at bagong buhay, habang tuluyang nanghina ang CPP-NPA-NDF sa ideolohiya at operasyon. Ang giyera kontra droga, bagamat kontrobersyal sa mata ng mga banyaga, ay nagligtas ng libo-libong pamilya mula sa kasamaan ng droga, winasak ang drug laboratories, nahuli ang mga drug lord, at nasamsam ang bilyon-bilyong halaga ng ilegal na droga. Nagpatupad siya ng massive anti-corruption campaign, kung saan libo ang nasuspinde, natanggal, at nasampahan ng kaso, kahit pa sila ay malalapit sa kapangyarihan. Pinirmahan niya ang mga batas tulad ng Universal Health Care Law, Free College Tuition Law, Malasakit Center Act, at pinatupad ang 8888 complaint hotline para mas madali ang pagreklamo ng taumbayan sa tiwaling serbisyo ng gobyerno. Naisabatas ang 10-year validity ng passport, 5 to 10-year driver’s license, at isinulong ang digitization ng government transactions para mas mabilis at episyente ang proseso. Sa larangan ng foreign policy, tumayo siya para sa soberanya ng Pilipinas, hindi siya sunod-sunuran sa Amerika o China. Ipinaglaban niya ang karapatan ng bansa sa West Philippine Sea habang iningatan ang diplomasya. Hindi siya nagpadaig sa International Criminal Court at ipinakita sa buong mundo na ang Pilipinas ay isang malayang bansa. Sa gitna ng lahat ng ito, napababa niya ang krimen, napaamo ang trapiko sa EDSA sa pamamagitan ng Bus Rapid Transit system, napakilos ang PNP at AFP na may disiplina, at muling pinaniwala ang sambayanang Pilipino na posible ang gobyernong may malasakit, aksyon, at tunay na serbisyo. Ang kanyang pamumuno ay hindi tungkol sa pa-pogi, kundi sa konkretong resulta. Si Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte ay hindi lamang naging lider kundi naging alamat, isang simbolo ng tapang, katapatan, at pagmamahal sa bayan na hinding-hindi mabubura sa kasaysayan.

WHERE IS THE PRESIDENT NOW?
While Typhoon Crising lashes the Philippines, leaving entire towns flooded, homes destroyed, and Filipinos crying for help, our President is abroad—comfortably meeting with the US President.
 This is leadership?
In the face of calamity, when his people need him the most, he chooses to leave. No direct presence, no leadership on the ground. Just silence. Is this the kind of leader we deserve?
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, the President is the Commander-in-Chief and must be present and accountable in times of national emergency. Leaving the country without declaring who is in command violates his constitutional duties.
 LEGAL BASIS: 
 Article VII, Section 4 – The President shall ensure the faithful execution of the laws and must uphold accountability to the people.
 Article XI, Section 1 – Public officers, including the President, must at all times be accountable to the people.
 Article XI, Section 2 – The President may be removed from office on impeachment for culpable violation of the Constitution, betrayal of public trust, or gross neglect of duty.
 Abandoning the nation during a declared State of Calamity without properly delegating emergency authority can be considered gross negligence and betrayal of public trust.
Is this the kind of leader we want — one who leaves during disaster? Or do we deserve someone who will stand and lead in the storm?

DALAWANG LPA SA LOOB AT LABAS NG PAR, PATULOY NGAYONG BINABANTAYAN 
Ang unang LPA (08a) na nasa silangan ng #Quezon ay patuloy na kumikilos papalapit sa landmass ng #Luzon. Inaasahang tuluyan na itong magla-landfall bukas ng gabi at inaasahang tatawirin ang kalupaan ng #NorthernLuzon hanggang sa Biyernes ng umaga.
Inaasahang bahagya rin nitong hahatakin ang #Habagat na inaasahang magdadala ng mga kalat-kalat na pag-ulan sa bansa partikular sa kanlurang bahagi.
Samantala, isa pang panibagong LPA (08b) ang nabuo sa labas ng PAR o sa silangan ng #NorthernLuzon at may tsansang pumasok ng PAR at maging bagyo sa mga susunod na araw. 
Sakaling maging bagyo ito pagpasok ng PAR, tatawagin itong #FabianPH.
Patuloy na babantayan ang magiging kilos nito dahil hindi rin inaalis ang posibilidad na lumapit ito sa #NorthernLuzon next week.
Manatiling mag-antabay ng mga susunod pang update hinggil sa mga nasabing sama ng panahon sa mga susunod na araw.
— PWS/PSU

Nag-atubang og daghang warrants of arrest sa Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 10 sa siyudad sa Davao ang kanhing pulis nga si Arturo Lascañas tungod sa mga kasong online libel, murder, ug attempted murder.
Labing uwahing warrant ni Lascañas mao ang online libel pinetsahan Hunyo 9, 2025 nga may pyansang P48,000.
Mga una niyang warrants, mao ang tungod sa kasong murder, pinetsahan Oktubre 16, 2020 nga wa’y pyansa. Laing kaso mai ang attempted murder nga may bail nga P120,000.

Kahinumduman nga si Lascañas, mipasiatab nga miyembro siya sa Davao Death Squad, ug alegasyong misibat pagawas sa nasud ug mitestigo batok former President Rodrigo Duterte.

ISSUED AT: 5:00 PM 15 August 2025

SYNOPSIS: Southwest Monsoon affecting Zamboanga Peninsula. Localized Thunderstorms affecting rest of Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Zamboanga Peninsula will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. Rest of Mindanao will be partly cloudy to cloudy with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from south to southwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.8 meters).

Ang Zamboanga Peninsula makasinati sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa katag katag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang mga pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto na sa usahay kusog nga mga pag-ulan. Ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa habagatang ngadto sa habagatang kasadpang nga direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud.

Sa kanyang ikaapat na SONA, ipinagmalaki ni Pangulong Ferdinand “Bongbong” R. Marcos, Jr. ang makabagong teknolohiya ng ating proyekto bilang epektibong bahagi ng disaster awareness at resilience sa tulong ng ating early warning system for landslides.
Ayon naman kay DOST Secretary Renato U. Solidum, Jr., hindi lang teknolohiya ang mahalaga kundi pati na rin ang malaking papel ng komunidad sa paggamit nito at pagsisiguro ng kanilang kaligtasan laban sa anumang panganib.
Patunay nito ang people-centered early warning system na 12 taon nang ipinapatupad ng proyekto, katuwang ang mga lokal na pamahalaan, pamayanan, at iba’t ibang ahensya sa buong bansa.
𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗮 𝘀𝗮 𝗯𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘁 𝗸𝗼𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗱 𝗻𝗮 𝗻𝗮𝘀𝗮 𝗽𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗿𝗼. 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗮 𝘀𝗮 𝗯𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗵𝗮𝘆.
Patuloy na maglilingkod ang 𝗗𝘆𝗻𝗮𝘀𝗹𝗼𝗽𝗲 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁 para sa inyo 24/7. Gaya ng paalala ng ating Pangulo, “Hindi tayo dapat tumigil sa ating mga ginagawang paghahanda, dahil ang banta ay patuloy na naririyan.”

Contractors for flood control projects across the Philippines appeared before the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee on Tuesday, August 19, 2025, for a probe into the nation’s flood management issues.
Alan Quirante of QM Builders, a Cebu-based development firm, was among the seven contractors who attended the inquiry. Four other contractors sent representatives, while seven more were absent but submitted written replies.
The Senate hearing followed a report from the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), released on August 11, which ranked Cebu second nationwide in the number of flood control projects despite not being among the country’s top 10 flood-prone provinces.
Based on the National Adaptation Plan of the Philippines 2023–2050, Cebu recorded 414 completed and ongoing flood control projects between July 2022 and May 2025 -- second only to Bulacan. Nationwide, a total of 9,855 projects are in place, amounting to more than P545 billion.
QM Builders is currently ranked as the country’s fourth-largest contractor. The PCO report stemmed from President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive during his June 28, 2025, State of the Nation Address. | via SunStar Cebu

Flood control isn’t just about drainage and infrastructure, but also about good governance, citizen education, and accountability. Flood control needs 4R - Responsibility, Reform, Restoration, and Results. Politicians, contractors, and citizens must be accountable—budgets and projects must be published, and corrupt officials jailed. Communities must be reformed through education on waste segregation, discipline, and disaster readiness. Nature must be restored by reforestation, tree planting, and protecting rivers and wetlands. Only then will we see real results: reduced flooding, stronger communities, and a government that truly serves the people. 1. Responsibility – Leaders and citizens must be accountable: publish budgets, complete projects, and jail corrupt politicians and contractors. 2. Reform – Educate communities on waste segregation, disaster preparedness, and discipline to prevent flooding. 3. Restoration – Reforest watersheds, plant trees, protect rivers, wetlands, and coastlines, and enforce environmental laws. 4. Results – Ensure transparency, monitor projects, and measure success in reduced flooding, healthier ecosystems, and resilient communities.

LOOK: RDRRMC1 PREPARES FOR #ISANGPH, CONDUCTS PDRA AND WEATHER UPDATING
In anticipation of the possible effects of the Tropical Depression (TD) #ISANGPH in Region I, the Regional Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council 1 (RDRRMC1) convened on 21 August 2025 for a Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment (PDRA) Scenario Building.
Further, on 22 August 2025, the council also convened for a weather updating to monitor the track and possible effects of TD #ISANGPH. DOST-PAGASA presented the weather forecast and dam updates, while DENR-MGB shared the landslide and flood susceptibility updates.
As of DOST-PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Bulletin No. 1, Tropical Cyclone Warning Signal (TCWS) No. 1 is raised for the provinces of Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, and Pangasinan. While based on the Weather Advisory No. 4, heavy rainfall is expected in the provinces of La Union and Pangasinan.
Moreover, based on the DENR-MGB R1, a total of 896 barangays across the provinces of Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, and Pangasinan are susceptible to landslide and flooding. 
With the possible effects of TD #ISANGPH, the RDRRMC1 member-agencies and the PDRRMCs of Region I are prepared and ready to respond to any eventualities that may occur.

PRESS STATEMENT
DOST-PAGASA S & T Media Service
Quezon City, 26 August 2025
LA NIÑA WATCH
LOOMING LA NIÑA CONDITIONS
DOST-PAGASA has been continuously monitoring the El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) in the tropical Pacific. ENSO-neutral is most likely to persist until the August-September-October 2025 season. However, model forecasts suggest an increasing probability of short-lived La Niña conditions as early as the September-October-November season until the October-November-December season.  
La Niña (cool phase of ENSO) is characterized by unusually cooler-than-average sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.  When conditions are favorable for the development of La Niña within the next six months and the probability is 55% or more, a La Niña Watch is issued.  
Historically, La Niña is characterized by an above-average number of tropical cyclone occurrences towards the end of the year and above-normal rainfall conditions in most parts of the country that can trigger adverse impacts, including floods and landslides in vulnerable areas. 
DOST-PAGASA will continue to closely monitor the possibility of La Niña conditions and its effect on the local climate. All concerned agencies and the public are encouraged to continue monitoring and take precautionary measures against their potential impacts. 
For more information, please call the Climate Monitoring and Prediction Section (CLIMPS), Climatology and Agrometeorology Division (CAD) at telephone number (02) 8284-0800 local 4920 and 4921 or through email: pagasa.climps@gmail.com.

DOST-PAGASA SITUATIONER
As of 8:00 AM today, the Low Pressure Area (LPA)  located 405km east of Hinatuan, Surigao del Sur has a high potential of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours.
The LPA will bring cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms over Eastern Visayas, Central Visayas, Caraga, Northern Mindanao, and Davao Region. ADVISORY TO FARMERS AND FISHERFOLK
The Department is advising farmers to observe and perform the following, as applicable:
1. Regularly monitor the latest local weather information and updates;
2. Harvest mature crops;
3. Secure seed reserves, planting materials, and other farm inputs in safe and proper storage areas; 
4. Relocate farm machineries, equipment, and other farm tools to higher ground;
5. Secure sufficient feeds and water for the possible relocation of animals; and
6. Clear drainage in irrigation and rice paddies from obstructions to prevent flooding and promote fast drainage of water.
Meanwhile, fisherfolk are advised to:
1. Secure fish cages, fish ponds, and fish stocks. Perform early harvest if needed and    mobilize post-harvest equipment and facilities; 
2. Secure fishing vessels in higher ground; 
3. Plan or dismiss sea travel as potentially rough conditions prevail over affected seaboards; and
4. Coordinate and follow fishing advisories from local authorities. A 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲, on the other hand, covers a 24-hour period but is issued only at the provincial level. It provides a broader outlook on potential weather disturbances but lacks the short-term accuracy of 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬. Since a 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲 is based on a 24-hour outlook, it should not be used as a basis for class suspensions or other official decisions. For class suspensions or other official decisions, please refer to 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 issued by the respective PAGASA Regional Services Divisions: Northern Luzon Prsd PAGASA-National Capital Region PRSD Pagasa Southern Luzon PAGASA Visayas PRSD Mindanao Prsd maulan po dito ngayon sa camsur

September 19, 2025 - The Office of Civil Defense Region X (OCD X) conducted a site inspection in Valencia City, Bukidnon after a flash flood on September 17, 2025 that affected more than 2,000 families.
OCD X Regional Director and Northern Mindanao Regional Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NorMin RDRRMC) Chairperson Antonio B. Sugarol led the team in coordinating response operations and met with Mayor Amie G. Galario and City DRRM Officer June Ray A. Valero to assess urgent needs.
At the request of the Valencia City LGU, OCD X facilitated the augmentation of three (3) Water Search and Rescue (WASAR) Teams consisting of Special Operations Group of the Philippine Coast Guard, Northern Mindanao, the Cagayan de Oro City DRRMD (CDO-CDRRMD) WASAR Team and 4ID, PA WASAR Team.
In coordination with the Tactical Operations Group 10, Philippine Air Force, two (2) Black Hawk helicopters airlifted the team from 4ID, PA. These teams will augment and assist in the ongoing search and retrieval operations as four (4) persons still remain missing.

DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. FORECAST:
Dinagat Islands and Surigao del Norte will experience rains with gusty winds due to Typhoon OPONG. Possible floods or landslides due to moderate to heavy rains to at times intense rains. Minimal to minor threat to life and property due to strong winds. Meanwhile Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao and the rest of Caraga will experience occasional rains due to the Southwest Monsoon. Possible flashfloods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. The rest of Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon (Habagat). Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Moderate to Strong winds from the southwest with moderate to rough seas (2.5 to 4.0 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang Dinagat Islands ug Surigao del Norte makasinati sa mga pag ulan ug kalit nga huros sa hangin tungod kang TY OPONG. Possible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto sa kusog ngadto sa usahay intense nga pag-ulan. Samtang ang Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao ug ubang dapit sa CARAGA makasinati sa katagkatag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagdalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili say uta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto sa usahay kusog nga pag-ulan. Ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto na sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Officialial Tropical Cyclone Advisory as of 5am, September 26, 2025
SEEK SHELTER NOW! Severe Tropical Storm #OpongPH (BUALOI) is over MASBATE!
Severe Tropical Storm OPONG has slightly weakened but remains a dangerous threat as it traverses the Philippine archipelago. Expect powerful winds, heavy rainfall, and a high risk of life-threatening storm surge.
 TCWS No. 3 in Effect!
Storm-force winds (89-117 km/h) are expected in:
LUZON: Sorsogon, Masbate (including Ticao and Burias Islands), Albay, portions of Camarines Sur/Quezon/Laguna, Marinduque, Romblon, Oriental/Occidental Mindoro, and Batangas.
VISAYAS: Northern Samar, Biliran, and central portions of Eastern Samar, Samar, and Leyte.
Potential Impact: Moderate to significant threat to life and property.
 TCWS No. 2 in Effect!
Gale-force winds (62-88 km/h) expected over:
Metro Manila, the rest of Bicol, Cavite, Rizal, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, and more parts of Southern Luzon and Western Visayas.
Potential Impact: Minor to moderate threat to life and property.
Current Status (5:00 AM, 26 September 2025):
Location: Vicinity of Palanas, Masbate.
Max Winds: 110 km/h | Gustiness: 150 km/h
Movement: West Northwestward at 30 km/h.
 COASTAL HAZARDS: EXTREME RISK!
LIFE-THREATENING STORM SURGE with peak heights exceeding 3.0 meters is highly possible within 36 hours across low-lying coastal areas of Zambales, Bataan, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Mindoro provinces, Bicol Region, and most of Visayas.
Sea Travel is RISKY for ALL TYPES of vessels over the seaboards of Southern Luzon and Visayas due to very rough to very high seas. Mariners must remain in port!
 HEAVY RAINFALL & MONSOON (HABAGAT) ENHANCEMENT:
Refer to Weather Advisory No. 27 for the full rainfall outlook.
The Southwest Monsoon (Habagat), enhanced by Opong, will bring strong to gale-force gusts to areas not under a Wind Signal, including the Ilocos Region, CAR, Cagayan Valley, and Palawan today.
FORECAST: OPONG will continue moving West Northwestward across Masbate, Sibuyan Sea, Southern CALABARZON, and Northern MIMAROPA before exiting to the West Philippine Sea tonight/tomorrow morning.
ACTION ITEMS:
Monitor updates closely. The next bulletin is at 8:00 AM today.
Execute evacuation plans if you are in high-risk zones for storm surge or flooding.
Secure homes and belongings. Do not leave your safety to chance.
SOURCE: DOST

Zamboanga Peninsula will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms caused by Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to heavy rains. Rest of Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds, from the northeast to southeast; with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5 meters).

Ang Zamboanga Peninsula makasinati sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa katagkatag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagdalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon/Habagat. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto sa usahay kusog nga pag-ulan. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa mga severe thunderstorms. 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗗: Severe Tropical Storm (STS) Opong caused massive destruction as it battered large parts of the Visayas and Bicol Region, leaving at least four people dead and displacing more than 360,000 families, or about 1.414 million individuals, due to flooding and landslides.
In its 11:00 p.m. bulletin, PAGASA reported that STS Opong was located 260 kilometers west of Calapan City, Oriental Mindoro, as it moved over the West Philippine Sea. It is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) this morning or by midday, heading toward the northern part of Vietnam with sustained winds of 110 kph and gusts of up to 135 kph.
According to the Office of Civil Defense (OCD), more than 87,000 residents in the Bicol Region evacuated, while around 73,000 individuals remain in evacuation centers in Eastern Samar and Northern Samar.
In Masbate, three fatalities were reported, including one crushed by a fallen tree, while another person in Camarines Norte was struck by lightning. Around 20,000 people were affected in Masbate, governor Richard Kho said.
The storm impacted 11 regions, particularly 46 provinces, 391 cities and municipalities, and 2,891 barangays.
Experts have long warned that typhoons are becoming stronger and more frequent due to global warming, resulting in more severe damage to vulnerable communities.
STS Opong struck just days after Super Typhoon Ragasa, which killed at least nine people and displaced thousands in Northern Luzon. The back-to-back disasters have made it more difficult for local governments to provide aid and repair damaged infrastructure.
Meanwhile, as the public struggles with the devastation brought by successive storms, a major controversy surrounds government flood control projects. Investigations suggest that some officials may have profited from multi-billion peso kickbacks, allegedly spent on lavish lifestyles instead of urgently needed infrastructure against disasters. The issue sparked massive protests on September 21, 2025, at Rizal Park in Manila and at the EDSA People Power Monument in Quezon City.
The impact of STS Opong goes beyond the loss of lives and properties, it also highlights the deeper issues the country faces, from the effects of climate change to corruption in projects that should have served as vital defenses against natural calamities.

THE LOW PRESSURE AREA EAST OF SOUTHERN LUZON DEVELOPED INTO TROPICAL DEPRESSION “PAOLO”.

The center of Tropical Depression PAOLO was estimated based on all available data at 760 km East of Virac, Catanduanes (14.1°N, 131.2°E).

Maximum sustained winds of 45 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 55 km/h, and central pressure of 1004 hPa
• Present Movement:
Westward at 25 km/h

Strong winds extend outwards up to 360 km from the center
TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNALS (TCWS) IN EFFECT
 ➣ No Wind Signal currently hoisted.
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
 ➣ Heavy Rainfall Outlook
PAOLO is less likely to directly affect the weather condition of the country in the next 24 hours. Onset of heavy rains due PAOLO is possible by Friday (03 October) onwards. A weather advisory may be released today in anticipation of the heavy rains that PAOLO may bring over Northern Luzon and portions of Central Luzon.
 ➣ Severe Winds
Wind Signal No. 1 may be hoisted over the eastern sections of Northern and Central Luzon as early as this afternoon or evening. The highest Wind Signal that will likely be hoisted throughout its passage is Wind Signal No. 3. However, since the possibility of reaching typhoon category before landfall is not ruled out, the worst case scenario is Wind Signal No. 4.
 ➣ Coastal Inundation
There is a potential risk of coastal flooding due to storm surge in low-lying coastal areas of Northern and Central Luzon due to the passage of PAOLO. Storm surge warning may be issued today or tomorrow (02 October).
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
 ➣ 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
PAOLO may bring moderate to rough seas over the coastal waters of Northern and Central Luzon starting Friday (03 October) early morning. Gale Warning may be raised over the seaboards of Northern and Central Luzon as early as tomorrow (02 October) afternoon in anticipation of rough to very rough sea conditions. 
TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
• PAOLO is forecast to move generally west northwestward for the entire forecast period. On the forecast track, PAOLO may make landfall over Isabela or northern Aurora on Friday (03 October) morning or afternoon. Further southward shift of track is possible depending on the strength of the high pressure area to the north of PAOLO.
• PAOLO will continue to intensify while over the Philippine Sea and may reach severe tropical storm category by Friday morning. Further intensification into a Typhoon prior to landfall is not ruled out. 
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. Persons living in areas identified to be highly or very highly susceptible to these hazards are advised to follow evacuation and other instructions from local officials. For heavy rainfall warnings, thunderstorm/rainfall advisories, and other severe weather information specific to your area, please monitor products issued by your local PAGASA Regional Services Division.
The next tropical cyclone bulletin will be issued at 5:00 PM today.

EARTHQUAKE RESPONSE UPDATE | Dagdag 12,700 Food Packs sa mga Apektado ng Lindol sa Cebu
Bilang tugon sa patuloy na pangangailangan ng mga apektadong pamilya, nagpadala ang DSWD ng karagdagang 12,700 kahon ng family food packs (FFPs) sa iba’t ibang bayan sa Cebu na matinding tinamaan ng magnitude 6.9 na lindol.
Kabilang sa nakatakdang padalhan ay ang Borbon (4,000 FFPs), Tabuelan (2,000 FFPs), Bantayan (2,000 FFPs), Medellin (2,000 FFPs), at Sogod (2,700 FFPs).

BAGYONG “PAOLO” MAGDADALA NG MALAKAS NA ULAN SA NUEVA VIZCAYA AT KALAPIT-LUGAR
Nagbabala ang PAGASA na asahan ang matinding pagbuhos ng ulan sa malaking bahagi ng Hilagang Luzon dala ng Severe Tropical Storm “Paolo”. Ayon sa Weather Advisory No. 6 na inilabas nitong Oktubre 2, 2025 alas-11 ng gabi, posibleng umabot sa 100 hanggang 200 milimetro ang ulan bukas hanggang gabi sa Nueva Vizcaya, kasama ang Cagayan, Kalinga, Mountain Province, Ifugao, Benguet, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan at Nueva Ecija. Mas malakas pa ang inaasahang ulan sa Isabela, Quirino at Aurora na maaaring lumampas sa 200 milimetro. Binalaan ng mga eksperto na mas mataas pa ang epekto sa mga kabundukan at matataas na lugar, na posibleng magdulot ng landslide at pagbaha.
Mula bukas ng gabi hanggang Sabado ng gabi, Oktubre 4, patuloy pa rin ang malalakas na ulan sa Ilocos Region, Benguet, Abra, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Zambales at Tarlac. Dahil dito, mahigpit na pinapayuhan ang mga residente at mga lokal na pamahalaan na magsagawa ng agarang paghahanda at sumunod sa mga abiso ng kani-kanilang DRRMO. Ipinaliwanag din ng PAGASA na ang Weather Advisory ay nagbibigay ng mas malawak na tanaw sa loob ng 24 oras, habang ang Heavy Rainfall Warning ay nakatuon sa susunod na tatlong oras gamit ang Doppler radar na mas eksakto para sa mga agarang desisyon tulad ng class suspensions at paglilikas. Metro Manila and Cebu City, Philippines — The Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau (DENR-MGB) has deployed an eight-member team of geologists, consisting of six from the Central Office and two from Regional Office VII, to conduct a comprehensive Post-Disaster Geohazards Assessment across several areas in Cebu Province. The assessment aims to identify zones susceptible to flooding, rain-induced landslides, ground subsidence, and sinkhole formation.
The initiative aims to enhance public safety and guide local government units (LGUs) in land-use planning and disaster risk reduction, particularly in communities situated on karst terrains characterized by limestone formations that are prone to dissolution and collapse.
According to Assistant Secretary for Mining Concerns and concurrent OIC Director Engr. Michael V. Cabalda, the assessment involves ground validation and geohazards data analysis. “This study will enable us to pinpoint areas susceptible to flooding, rain-induced landslides, and those areas with high potential for ground subsidence and provide technical recommendations to LGUs for proper zoning, building regulation, and emergency preparedness,” the Engr. Cabalda said.

HOW CAN WE #MAKEPANGASINANLIVEABLE?
Around 134 Pangasinenses gathered on Thursday, October 2, at the Lay Formation Center in Dagupan City for Rappler’s #MakePangasinanLiveable public forum. 
Local officials, community leaders, and citizens came together to talk about urgent concerns in the community, including flooding, education, healthcare, public safety, and good governance, and what can be done together to address them.
The public forum is part of Rappler’s civic empowerment roadshow, “#AmbagNatin: Engage for Change,” which aims to bring people and institutions together to shape better communities from the ground up.
This Pangasinan leg was organized in partnership with the Archdiocese of Lingayen-Dagupan and the AB English Language program of Pangasinan State University Lingayen Campus, with food sponsorship by Mang Inasal.

Isang malakas na aftershock ang naramdaman ng mga residente sa #NorthernCebu bandang 5:41 pm, Sabado, October 4, 2025. 
Sapul sa CCTV sa Brgy. Don Gregorio Antigua, Borbon, #Cebu ang malakas na pagyanig na umabot sa magnitude 4.6 na lindol. 
Naramdaman din ito sa iba pang bahagi ng northern #Cebu, maging sa #NegrosOccidental, #Leyte, at #SouthernLeyte.
Ayon sa PHIVOLCS, inaasahang magtatagal pa ang mga AFTERSHOCKS sa mga susunod na araw, linggo, o kahit buwan.
Patuloy na pinag-iingat ang ating mga kababayan na mga Cebuano dahil sa mga pinsalang maaaring idulot pa ng mga pagyanig.

As rains continue to flood parts of the country, health experts are sounding the alarm on leptospirosis — a serious infection that can be life-threatening if not treated early.
The Pediatric Nephrology Society of the Philippines, a group of local kidney specialists for kids, recently shared tips on how to spot and prevent leptospirosis, especially in children.
What is leptospirosis?
It’s a disease you can get by:
 Wading in floodwater
 Drinking water contaminated with rat urine or waste from other infected animals
 The bacteria (called leptospira) can enter your body through:
Open wounds
Scratches or broken skin soaked in floodwater
 Symptoms to watch out for:
Fever
Headache
Stomach pain
Red eyes
Yellowing of the skin (jaundice)
Trouble peeing
Shortness of breath
 Preventive meds you should know about:
If your child has waded through floodwater even just once, here’s what the experts recommend:
 Doxycycline 100 mg (2 tablets within 24 hours) — available for free at health centers
 Azithromycin (10 mg/kg single dose, max 500 mg)
 Amoxicillin (50 mg/kg/day, every 6 hours for 3–5 days, max 500 mg per dose)
If exposure happened over 7 days ago, they should take medicine again after a week.
OpinYonistas, avoid floodwater if you can.

Uploader Filipina Maloto shared a video showing a bunch of balloons for sale accidentally floating away.
She looked for “Nanay,” the vendor often seen in front of the church in Concepcion, Marikina, bought some of her remaining balloons, and paid P1,000 to help out.
Nanay explained that she accidentally let go of the balloons while assisting a customer. “Bayaran pa naman ng bahay. Maiyak-iyak na ko talaga, pero nilalakasan ko lang ‘yung loob ko,” she said.
“Ang sabi ko po, sa kaniya na ‘yung sukli. Tapos ayun, sobrang saya ni Nanay napaiyak na kami parehas kasi ‘di siya makapaniwala,” the uploader recalled.
Meanwhile, the story touched many, inspiring donations of cash and groceries for Nanay.

“Ang Di‐Inaasahang Lindol sa Mindanao Kaninang Umaga”
Kanina lang umaga, isang malakas na lindol na may tinatayang magnitude 7.4 (o mas mataas pa sa ilang pagtataya) ang yumanig sa rehiyon ng Mindanao, lalong-lalo na sa baybayin ng Davao Oriental malapit sa bayan ng Manay. 
 Nagdulot ito ng pagyanig sa lupa sa maraming lugar, pagbagsak o pagbitak ng mga pader at gusali, pagkasira sa ospital, at pagka‐evacuate sa mga pasyente. 
 Mga coastal areas ay nilisan pansamantala dahil sa banta ng tsunami, bagaman kalaunan ay binawi ang tsunami alert. 
The Guardian
 Sa ngayon, kumpirmado nang may dalawang patay sa Davao Oriental dahil sa pagbagsak ng gusali. 
 Mysterious / Teoretikal na Pagsusuri
Pag‐galaw sa Philippine Trench
May teorya na ang lindol ay nagmula sa paggalaw ng isang segment sa Philippine Trench, isang lugar kung saan nagtatagpo ang mga tectonic plates sa ilalim ng dagat. 
 Ang ganitong pag‐galaw ay maaaring magtulak ng seabed pataas o pababa—na siya namang puwedeng magpagalaw ng tubig sa ibabaw, na nagiging sanhi ng tsunami. 
Submarine Landslides
Isang posibilidad ay may pagguho sa ilalim ng dagat (submarine landslide) na nangyari dahil sa malakas na get-o galaw ng lupa sa ilalim ng dagat. Ang ganitong pagguho ay puwedeng maglatag ng dagdag na gibain sa pagtaas o pagbaba ng tubig sa baybayin. Ito’y mas subtle at mahirap mapansin agad.
Aftershocks / Chain Reaction
Dahil dati’y nagkaroon ng malalakas na lindol sa iba’t ibang bahagi ng Pilipinas nitong mga nakaraang araw (halimbawa sa Cebu) 
, may posibilidad na ang stress sa mga fault lines ay nag‐accumulate. Kapag may lindol sa isang bahagi, maaaring magkaroon ito ng domino effect sa katabing faults.
Fault Complexity / Hidden Faults
Posible ring may hindi pa natutuklasang pinagsisikipan o fault line sa ilalim ng dagat o sa karatig na lupain. Sa ilang malalakas na lindol sa kasaysayan, lumitaw na may bahagi ng fault na hindi pa nakikita o hindi pa nailalarawan ng mga geologists.
Anomalous Phenomena / Sigaw ng Kalikasan
Sa aspetong “misteryoso,” may mga naniniwala rin sa mga sinaunang paniniwala—na ang lindol ay senyales mula sa kalikasan, o reaksyon sa masyadong labis na pagsamantala sa lupa, deforestation, pagmimina, o pagbabago sa ilalim ng dagat. Hindi ito sang‐ayon sa agham, ngunit madalas lumalabas sa mga lokal na kuwento at teoryang popular paminsan-minsan.
 Disclaimer (Para sa Edukasyunal na Layunin Lamang)
Ang nilalaman dito ay teoretikal at circumstantial lamang—hindi ito opisyal na ulat mula sa Phivolcs o iba pang mapagkakatiwalaang ahensya. Huwag ituring ito bilang huling hatol o totoong paliwanag. Para sa mas tamang impormasyon, mangyaring sumangguni sa Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) o lokal na awtoridad sa agham at kalikasang sakuna.

Baha ito ng sariling pagkukulang,
Hindi ng langit, hindi ng kalikasan.
Basura sa kanal, siksik sa daan,
Itinapon ng taong walang pakialam.
Hindi Diyos ang dahilan ng unos,
Kundi kawalang-disiplina at palusot.
Pondo’y nawala, proyekto’y naantala,
Pero sa TV, puro pangakong maganda.
Kaya’t huwag tayong magtaka,
Kung taon-taon tayo’y lumulubog sa baha.
Sapagkat ang kalaban, hindi ulan —
Kundi ang ating sariling kapabayaan.

WHERE IS THE PRESIDENT NOW?
While Typhoon Crising lashes the Philippines, leaving entire towns flooded, homes destroyed, and Filipinos crying for help, our President is abroad—comfortably meeting with the US President.
 This is leadership?
In the face of calamity, when his people need him the most, he chooses to leave. No direct presence, no leadership on the ground. Just silence. Is this the kind of leader we deserve?
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, the President is the Commander-in-Chief and must be present and accountable in times of national emergency. Leaving the country without declaring who is in command violates his constitutional duties.
 LEGAL BASIS: 
 Article VII, Section 4 – The President shall ensure the faithful execution of the laws and must uphold accountability to the people.
 Article XI, Section 1 – Public officers, including the President, must at all times be accountable to the people.
 Article XI, Section 2 – The President may be removed from office on impeachment for culpable violation of the Constitution, betrayal of public trust, or gross neglect of duty.
 Abandoning the nation during a declared State of Calamity without properly delegating emergency authority can be considered gross negligence and betrayal of public trust.
Is this the kind of leader we want — one who leaves during disaster? Or do we deserve someone who will stand and lead in the storm?

Senator Bam Aquino's Philippine National Budget Blockchain Bill captured public attention, especially given the timing around flood-control controversies. The current outrage has ignited an important conversation on how public funds are spent-- and potentially hidden. In the uproar over stalled projects and missing allocations, the bill promised a clean fix: put every peso on the blockchain. Each transaction, it claimed, would live forever on an immutable ledger—visible to all, tamper-proof, and honest by design. It’s a seductive vision: that technology could finally do what politics hasn’t.
But that’s the problem. We keep mistaking technology for reform. Blockchain is treated as the cure, not the tool. As if corruption were a software bug, not a symptom of power, discretion, and inequality. The assumption is that when code is incorruptible, people will become so too. Yet history reminds us that tools inherit their makers’ hands—and their habits.

Ramil intensifies into a tropical storm.
Wind signal no. 2 is now up over Camarines Norte, Catanduanes, and northern Camarines Sur.

TROPICAL STORM RAMIL MAKES LANDFALL IN SORSOGON; HEAVY RAINS THREATEN LUZON AND VISAYAS
Tropical Storm Ramil (international name: Fengshen) has officially made landfall in southeastern Luzon, near Sorsogon and the Bicol Region, after tracking slightly farther south and west than early forecasts predicted.
Now moving slowly westward, Ramil is expected to cross the Bicol Region before heading toward Southern and Central Luzon, including areas near Metro Manila and Pangasinan, throughout the weekend.
PAGASA has raised Signal No. 2 over parts of Northern Samar and the eastern coast. However, the main concern is heavy rainfall, not wind — with 100 to 200 mm expected along the east coast and 50 to 150 mm across Bicol, Samar, and eventually much of Luzon.
Residents are warned of localized flooding and landslides, especially in mountainous and low-lying areas. Even regions north of the storm’s center may experience widespread rain due to its broad convection.
Authorities urge the public to stay alert and not focus solely on the storm’s center track, as outer rainbands often cause the most significant impacts.

𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: The key difference between a 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 and a 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲 lies in their forecast period, coverage areas, and accuracy. A 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 provides forecasts for the next three hours and applies up to the municipal level. It is more precise as it utilizes Doppler radar technology to track real-time rainfall intensity, making it highly effective for immediate decision-making in flood-prone areas. A 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲, on the other hand, covers a 24-hour period but is issued only at the provincial level. It provides a broader outlook on potential weather disturbances but lacks the short-term accuracy of 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬. For class suspensions or other official decisions, please refer to 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 issued by the respective PAGASA Regional Services Divisions.
